## Natural history notes

A medium-sized sallow moth characterized by mottled gray, brown, and tan forewings with pale looping marks that can resemble a figure-eight pattern. In Florida, it is found in hardwood hammocks, mixed forests, forest edges, parks, and other wooded habitats where oaks and related host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on oak and other hardwood foliage, helping move tree leaves into the broader food web as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitic wasps.
